[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Peter was born in 1740.  He passed away in 1812.

Erected by JOHN and JAMES GLASGOW in MEMORY of PETER GLASGOW their father, late Tenant Whitebank, who died the 7th Novr. 1812, aged 72 years.
Also JEAN ANDERSON his Spouse, who died 7 Jan. 1809, aged 73 years.
THREE of their Children, who died young.
== Research Notes ==
=== Whitebank trial identification — 30 October 2026 ===
The trial index names Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, tried on 9 October 1797. The held memorial transcription for Peter Glasgow-2878 calls him the late tenant of Whitebank, records death on 7 November 1812 aged 72, names Jean Anderson as spouse, and sons John and James as erectors. Matching personal name and the specific tenancy provide a substantially better identification than the Bathgate Peter-1466 comparison, which has no Whitebank link. Prefer Peter-2878 as the trial subject at 94% subjective identity confidence. This is one memorial, also indexed under Jean, not two independent witnesses.

The original memorial image and court papers were not newly inspected. The trial index gives no age, family or occupation; another Peter of the same holding remains possible. The index records a guilty verdict and transportation sentence, not proof of a voyage, destination, actual removal, return or pardon. Do not use this occurrence to infer either man’s parents, alter Peter-1466’s 79% father assessment, or transfer the unassigned 1818 Edinburgh burial. Reassessment of held memorial evidence combined with a fresh index read, not newly discovered court papers.<ref name="WhitebankTrial1797">[https://www.scottishindexes.com/jcdetail.aspx?jcid=1797040&pid=179704079 Scottish Indexes, High Court of Justiciary Trial Papers], Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, 9 October 1797, NRS JC26/1797/40; index checked 30 October 2026. Original court papers not inspected.</ref><ref name="WhitebankMemorial">[https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/198800998/peter_glasgow Peter Glasgow memorial 198800998] and [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/198800999/jean-glasgow Jean Anderson memorial 198800999], held transcription of one shared Stichill stone, not two witnesses. The stone calls Peter the late tenant of Whitebank; original photograph not newly inspected.</ref>


=== Recorded Polwarth household — 11 November 2026 ===
The Peter/Petter Glasgow and Jean Anderson couple in the 1770 Swinton, 1772 Swinton and 1779 Polwarth indexes is identified with this memorial couple at 92% subjective confidence. Their son James was born 29 May 1779 and baptised 6 June at Polwarth; his later identity remains unresolved. The repeated full parental names, sons John and James named on the memorial, regional setting and adult ages support the household identification. Repeated indexes of a baptism are one event, not independent witnesses.<ref>[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/60143/records/644438 Ancestry, Scotland Select Births and Baptisms, James Glasgow, born 29 May and baptised 6 June 1779, Polwarth; Petter Glasgow and Jean Anderson]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4884269&tab=this Findmypast, John born 28 August and baptised 9 September 1772, Swinton, parents Peter Glasgow and Jean Anderson, OPR 755/1 item 8 p.24]. Held derivative transcripts; originals uninspected.</ref>

=== Possible parents and Patrick childhood — 11 November 2026 ===
Prefer [[Glasgow-1238|James Glasgow]] as a possible father at 45%, replacing the selected John-1444 hypothesis at 15%; retain [[Glasgow-1444|John Glasgow]] as an unselected alternative. [[Tait-2506|Elizabath Tait]] is separately selected as a possible mother at 45% from her literal maternal role. This depends on identifying Peter with [[Glasgow-1225|Patrick Glasgow]], baptised at Stichill on 20 June 1742 to James and Elizabath. The memorial age suggests about 1740; a delayed baptism or age error could fit, but is not proved. Peter/Patrick can occur as name alternatives, which admits this candidate without proving identity. No adult household record links Patrick to Jean Anderson’s husband. No merge, changed birth date or claim that Peter and Patrick were distinct brothers is made.<ref>[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/60143/records/12157281 Ancestry, Scotland Select Births and Baptisms, Patrick Glasgow, 20 June 1742, Stichill, James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_690838710&tab=this Findmypast R_690838710, same baptism]; [https://www.whatsinaname.net/male-names/Peter.html What’s in a Name, Peter, synonym Patrick], general naming context only. Original parish pages and stone not newly inspected.</ref>
